envelope.description: Implement the pure reconcileConfig module with a named catalog-error type

body.title: Implement the pure reconcileConfig module with a named catalog-error type
body.summary: Add src/config/reconcile.ts exporting `ConfigReconcileResult { config, changed, carried, filled, repaired }` and `reconcileConfig(existing: unknown, catalog: readonly ConfigOption[] = CONFIG_CATALOG): ConfigReconcileResult`. Strictly pure — no fs, IPC, socket or clock — because the daemon-boot caller runs before the socket exists (src/daemon/index.ts:178, DB opens only at :213). Build the output as a MERGE over a deep clone of `existing`, never a rebuild from catalog rows, so catalog-unenumerable keys survive blindly. Own the dot-path get/set walk inside this module (no reusable helper exists); mirror the ancestor-collision rule already inlined in the config.write handler at src/daemon/index.ts:1137-1139, strengthened with `!Array.isArray(...)` in the plain-object predicate, and record the discarded scalar in the repair record so callers can name the loss. The type-match predicate is a 4-arm exhaustive switch over the confirmed closed union 'string'|'number'|'boolean'|'enum'; note explicitly in a comment that 'enum' rows carry no allowed-values field so their predicate degenerates to `typeof === 'string'` (7 of 41 rows). Existence is tested with hasOwnProperty, never truthiness; null is rejected for object/string rows. Settling open question s8-cd3: the two catalog-integrity failures — a catalog row with an out-of-domain `type`, and a catalog row whose own default fails its own predicate — throw a dedicated exported `ConfigCatalogError extends Error` carrying the offending catalog path, distinct from every I/O and parse failure, so downstream callers can report a programmer error in our shipped catalog differently from a user-config or filesystem error. `carried`/`filled`/`repaired` carry dot-paths (repairs also carry the discarded value) so callers can log per-key detail. Derive `changed` from the same comparison that built the document. Land it unwired and inert.
acceptanceChecks: `reconcileConfig` is exported from src/config/reconcile.ts and the module imports nothing from node:fs, node:net, the daemon IPC layer, or any clock source
`existing` is never mutated: a deep-frozen input reconciles without throwing and deep-equals itself afterwards

Catalog keys absent from `existing` land in `filled` with the catalog default written; present-and-type-valid keys land in `carried` with the value referentially preserved; present-but-type-invalid keys land in `repaired` with the default substituted
filled/carried/repaired entries carry the catalog dot-path, and each repair entry additionally carries the discarded prior value (including the replaced scalar in the ancestor-collision case)
Non-object `existing` (undefined, null, array, string, number, boolean) is treated as {} — all catalog keys filled, nothing thrown
changed === (filled.length + repaired.length > 0), and changed === false implies result.config deep-equals existing

An out-of-domain catalog `type`, and a catalog row whose default fails its own declared type, each throw a `ConfigCatalogError` (not a bare Error) naming the offending catalog path; no user-config or I/O condition can produce that class
The type-match switch is exhaustive over the ConfigOption discriminant (a new member produces a compile error, not a silent pass-through)

tests.name: module surface — src/config/reconcile.ts exports reconcileConfig, ConfigReconcileResult and ConfigCatalogError, and its import specifiers include no node:fs, node:net, daemon IPC or clock source
result shape — filled/carried/repaired entries carry catalog dot-paths and every repair record carries the discarded prior value
